[[Tampa, Florida]] | former_school(s)= | career_highlights = Y | awards = | honors = * 2x ACC Defensive Player of the Year (2011, 2012) * First team All-ACC (2012) | records = | championships = Y | championship_list = | championship_list = *2011 ACC Regular-season *2012 ACC Regular-season | tournaments = Y | tournament_list = *[[2011 National Invitation Tournament|2010 NIT]] *[[2011 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2011 NCAA]] *[[2012 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2012 NCAA]] }} '''John Allen Henson''' (born December 28, 1990) is a college basketball player who currently plays for the [[North Carolina Tar Heels]]. He played high school basketball at [[Sickles High School]] in [[Tampa, Florida]].[http://tarheelblue.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/henson_john00.html TarHeelBlue.com John Henson Profile] Henson is listed at 6'11", 220 lb and has a 7'6" wingspan helping him become a dominant defensive player.[http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/player/_/id/45531/john-henson ESPN John Henson profile] ==Early life== Born in [[Greensboro, North Carolina]], Henson is the son of Matt and Annette Henson. His father played basketball at [[Norfolk State Spartans football|Norfolk State University]]. ==High school career== For three years, Henson attended [[Round Rock High School]] in [[Round Rock, Texas]]. His senior year, Henson transferred to [[Sickles High School]] in [[Tampa, Florida]]. Henson wore the jersey number 33, averaging 17.6 points, 12.2 rebounds, and 6.1 blocks per game as a senior in 2008-09. He scored a season-high 29 points against [[Tampa Bay Technical High School|Tampa Bay Tech]] and blocked 10 or more shots five times with a high of 11 on four occasions as a senior as well. Henson led the team to a 24-5 record and a perfect 10-0 league record,[http://www.maxpreps.com/athletes/2C3lBzDbuEqK_1674BWFQA/basketball-winter-08-09/stats-john-henson.htm MaxPreps John Henson Profile] but the team lost to [[Lakeland Senior High School (Lakeland, Florida)|Lakeland]] 48-43 in the regional seminfinals for the Florida FHSAA Class 6A championship.[http://www.fhsaa.org/sites/default/files/orig_uploads/sports/basketball-boys/archives/2008-09/brak6.htm 2009 Allstate FHSAA Class 6A Boys Basketball Championship Bracket] Henson was a first-team all-state selection and Tampa Bay Coaches Association Player of the Year. He played in the [[McDonald's All-American Game]] and the [[Nike Hoop Summit]]. He also earned first-team All-America honors from [[Parade (magazine)|Parade magazine]]. ==Recruitment== Henson was a highly-sought after forward, and was rated by [[Scout.com]] as the #1 power forward and the #4 overall player in the 2009 recruiting class.[http://scouthoops.scout.com/a.z?s=75&p=9&c=4&cfg=bb&yr=2009 Scout.com College Basketball Team Recruiting Prospects 2009] Analysts predicted he would be an important addition to what some thought would be the best frontcourt in the nation for the 2009-2010 season. When asked to evaluate Henson, head coach [[Roy Williams (coach)|Roy Williams]] said Henson had "tremendously long arms", and predicted he would "probably block more shots than any perimeter player in college basketball."[http://tarheelblue.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/101109aab.html 2009-10 Tar Heel Season Preview - Tarheelblue.com] ==College career== ===Freshman season=== Henson started the season at small forward for the [[2009–10 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|2009-10 Tar Heels]], but with the season-ending injury to [[Ed Davis (basketball)|Ed Davis]], Henson moved to power forward in mid-February 2010. After the move, Henson's performance improved, and he averaged 9.4 points per game in the last 16 contests of the season. However, the Tar Heels missed the [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship|NCAA tournament]], losing to the [[Dayton Flyers men's basketball|Dayton]] in the [[National Invitation Tournament|NIT]] finals [http://scores.espn.go.com/ncb/recap/_/id/300912168/boxscore?gameId=300912168 2010 NIT Championship Recap - ESPN.com] ===Sophomore season=== Henson was the winner of the ACC Defensive Player of the Year Award for 2011 and 2012. ===Junior season=== After North Carolina played Michigan State in the Carrier Classic, which took place on the flight deck of the USS Carl Vinson, Henson gave his jersey to a "wounded veteran" who was in attendance. Less than a week later, the jersey appeared on eBay.[http://www.webpronews.com/the-journey-of-john-hensons-game-worn-jersey-2011-11 The Journey of John Henson’s Game-Worn Jersey] Once Henson learned of the auction, he took to his Twitter account where he shared his feelings on the matter.[http://twitter.com/#!/_John_Henson_/status/136470575035072513 John Henson's Tweet] {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | align="left" | [[2009–10 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|2009–10]] | align="left" | [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]] | 37 || 12 || 15.8 || .486 || .222 || .438 || 4.4 || 0.9 || 0.7 || 1.6 || 5.7 {{S-end}}[http://stats.washingtonpost.com/cbk/players.asp?id=88219 Washington Post John Henson Profile] ==NBA career== Henson announced that he was entering the [[2012 NBA Draft]] along with [[Kendall Marshall]], [[Tyler Zeller]] and [[Harrison Barnes]]. ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *[http://tarheelblue.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/henson_john00.html TarHeelBlue.com Profile] *[http://northcarolina.scout.com/a.z?c=1&p=8&nid=3164671&s=78 Scout.com Profile] {{Persondata | NAME = Henson, John | ALTERNATIVE NAMES = | SHORT DESCRIPTION = American basketball player | DATE OF BIRTH = December 28, 1990 | PLACE OF BIRTH = [[Greensboro, NC]] | DATE OF DEATH = | PLACE OF DEATH = }} {{DEFAULTSORT:Henson, John}} [[Category:1990 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:African-American basketball players]] [[Category:McDonald's High School All-Americans]] [[Category:North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball players]] [[Category:Parade High School All-Americans (boys' basketball)]] [[Category:Power forwards (basketball)]]
